pages.text: FY 2025-26 reflects Persistent’s continued commitment to financial discipline, operational excellence, and sustainable value creation. Despite a dynamic macroeconomic environment characterised by geopolitical uncertainties, currency fluctuations, and evolving market conditions, we remained focused on executing our strategic priorities, investing prudently, and driving operational efficiencies. These efforts enabled us to deliver strong financial performance while further strengthening our balance sheet. Navigating Uncertainty with Discipline The technology industry continued to operate amid heightened uncertainty during the year, shaped by geopolitical tensions, including the conflict in the Middle East, supply chain disruptions, currency volatility, and the rapid emergence of AI-led disruption across the technology landscape. As enterprises reassessed investment priorities and accelerated the adoption of AI-powered solutions, the industry experienced significant shifts in demand patterns, operating models, and competitive dynamics. Against this backdrop, Persistent remained focused on executing its growth strategy with discipline and agility. By proactively investing in AI capabilities, strengthening our talent base, and aligning our offerings with evolving client priorities, we successfully sustained our growth momentum while adapting to a rapidly changing market environment. Our disciplined approach to capital allocation balanced strategic investments, ESG commitments, and fiscal prudence, enabling us to enhance operational efficiency, strengthen our market position, and deliver sustainable financial outcomes. These efforts not only helped us navigate an increasingly complex business environment but also positioned us to capitalise on the transformative opportunities emerging from the AI-driven evolution of the industry, reinforcing our foundation for long-term growth and value creation. Strengthening Performance Through Operational Excellence At Persistent, our culture of financial discipline is underpinned by a relentless focus on productivity and efficiency. During the year, we accelerated the adoption of AI, automation, and digitalisation across our operations, enabling greater scalability and improved cost management. We also enhanced utilisation levels and implemented targeted pricing initiatives, which contributed to improved operating leverage. Additionally, the depreciation of the Indian rupee provided a favourable tailwind. Together, these factors strengthened our profitability profile and supported margin expansion. As a result, we delivered an EBIT margin of 15.6%, despite absorbing a one-time impact of 0.6% related to the New Labour Code. This performance remains aligned with our long- term objective of maintaining EBIT margins in the 16%–17% range. Delivering Strong Financial Results Persistent delivered another year of robust growth, with total revenue increasing 23.5% to INR 147,484 Million. Growth was broad- based, supported by strong execution across all industry verticals. Profitability outpaced revenue growth, driven by continued operational efficiencies and disciplined cost management. Persistent Systems Limited has established structured mechanisms to inform customers of any potential risk of disruption or discontinuation of services. Delivery risks are jointly assessed with customers on a monthly basis, evaluated using a Risk Priority Number (RPN) and aggregated at the project level, with projects crossing defined thresholds classified as high or critical risk and reviewed fortnightly with senior delivery leadership. Risks and mitigation plans are proactively communicated through weekly status reports, monthly and quarterly business reviews, CXO to CXO interactions, and business continuity plans, with designated client contacts in place for escalations. These practices support transparency, timely mitigation, and continuity of essential services, and are complemented by strong client satisfaction outcomes in delivery and project management 4. Global Business Outlook The global economy enters Financial Year 2025-26 against a backdrop of slowing growth and renewed inflationary pressure. These conditions are linked to last year’s trade barriers and elevated uncertainty, with ongoing conflict in the Middle East compounding the strain. The challenges are particularly acute for emerging markets and developing economies, which remain more vulnerable to external shocks and financial instability. While increased defense spending in response to geopolitical tension may provide a temporary boost to economic activity, it also intensifies inflationary pressure and strains fiscal health, raising the likelihood of social unrest in fragile regions. The overall outlook remains clouded by substantial downside risks, including prolonged conflict, deepening geopolitical fragmentation and the resurgence of protectionist trade policies. In this volatile environment, organisations are under pressure to strike a careful balance between cost efficiency and the need to build resilience, agility and progress toward climate objectives, especially as regulatory frameworks grow more complex and unpredictable. At the same time, rapid advances in automation and artificial intelligence are helping to reduce operational workloads, but these technologies require strong governance structures and proactive workforce reskilling to ensure successful integration. As your Company looks to 2026 and 2027, the pace of disruption is accelerating, with technology companies moving from experimental AI pilots to large-scale, ROI-focused deployments that prioritise safety, security and regulatory compliance, while also laying the groundwork for the adoption of transformative quantum technologies. Company Outlook Your Company is a premier global provider of digital engineering and enterprise modernisation services. With more than 27,500 employees across 21 countries, it specialises in AI-driven solutions and software product engineering for industries such as BFSI, Healthcare and Hi-Tech, with deep expertise in building software products from conception to deployment. Its focus is on embedding AI-driven solutions across platforms, helping enterprises move from technical debt to competitive differentiation through a platform mindset. Your company’s strategic approach centers on AI readiness through modern technology and data stacks, enabling clients to become value creators. It modernises core platforms and embeds AI across operations, aligning modernisation with strategic priorities to accelerate product launches, improve cost-to-income ratios and build customer trust. From product engineering to cloud and AI-powered automation, your Company drives smarter, safer and more sustainable industrial ecosystems. Its expertise in building next-generation software products at speed, with breakthrough operational efficiency, continues to be valued by its clients and its focus on delivering insights-driven, omnichannel customer experiences using best-in-class technologies underpins the long-term relationships it sustains with most of its customers. Building the AI-led Enterprise For most enterprises, the question is no longer whether to adopt Generative AI, but where AI creates genuine value and where greater autonomy introduces risk. The market is shifting decisively from experimentation to disciplined, large-scale production. Generative AI is now firmly established from pilot to deployment, toward Agentic AI woven into core business processes. Yet realising AI’s full potential remains demanding. Integrating intelligence with existing enterprise systems is both complex and expensive and outcomes must be governed, secure and dependable at scale. Your Company’s AI strategy is anchored on three reinforcing pillars, underpinned by Responsible AI. Engineering Hyper-Productivity embeds AI across the software development lifecycle, so engineering teams deliver faster, raise quality and do more with less. Business Hyper-Productivity applies AI to automate and optimise business process workflows and decision-making across enterprise functions, enabling organisations to drive efficiency and faster outcomes. Enterprise Data Readiness prepares the enterprise data foundation, with the right structure, governance and accessibility so AI can deliver accurate, contextual and trusted outcomes at scale. Together, these pillars define the path enterprises must take to realise the full value of AI. Success lies in the last mile, making AI-driven outcomes repeatable, transparent and governed at scale, so that the desired business outcome is sustained and trusted across the enterprise. Notes forming part of consolidated financial statements The carrying amount of deferred tax asset is reviewed at each reporting date and reduced to the extent that it is no longer probable that sufficient taxable profit will be available against which such deferred tax assets can be realised. Deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities are offset, if a legally enforceable right exists to set off current tax assets against current tax liabilities and the deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities relate to the same taxable entity and the same taxation authority. Deferred tax relating to items recognised outside the consolidated statement of profit and loss is recognised in co-relation to the underlying transaction either in OCI or directly in equity. m. Segment reporting i. Identification of segment The Group’s operations predominantly relate to providing software products, services and technology innovation covering full life cycle of product to its customers. The components of the Group that engage in business activities from which they earn revenue and incur expenses, whose operating results are regularly reviewed by the Group’s Chief Operating Decision Maker, are identified as operating segments. ii. Allocation of income and direct expenses Income and direct expenses allocable to segments are classified based on items that are individually identifiable to that segment such as salaries, project related travel expenses etc. The remainder is considered as un-allocable expense and is charged against the total income. iii. Unallocated items Unallocated items include general corporate income and expense items which are not allocated to any business segment. Segregation of assets, liabilities, depreciation and amortisation and other non-cash expenses into various reportable segments have not been presented except for trade receivables and unbilled revenue as these items are used interchangeably among segments and the Group is of the view that it is not practical to reasonably allocate these items to individual segments and an ad-hoc allocation will not be meaningful. iv. Inter-segment transfers There are no inter-segments transactions. v. Segment accounting policies The Group prepares its segment information in conformity with accounting policies for preparing and presenting the consolidated financial statements of the Group as a whole. n. Earnings per share (EPS) Basic earnings per share are calculated by dividing the net profit for the year attributable to equity shareholders of the parent company by the weighted average number of equity shares outstanding during the year. The weighted average number of equity shares outstanding during the reporting period is adjusted for events such as bonus issue, bonus element in a rights issue, share split, and reverse share split (consolidation of shares), if any occurred during the reporting period, that have changed the number of equity shares outstanding, without a corresponding change in resources. For the purpose of calculating diluted earnings per share, the net profit for the year attributable to the equity shareholders of parent company and the weighted average number of equity shares outstanding during the year, are adjusted for the effects of all dilutive potential equity shares. The number of shares and potential dilutive equity shares are adjusted retrospectively for all periods presented for any bonus shares issues including for changes effected prior to the approval of the consolidated financial statements by the Board of Directors. o. We achieved a healthy revenue growth of 7.8% quarter-on-quarter and 20% year-on-year delivering USD 487.6 million in Q2 FY27. This marks our 26th sequential quarter of revenue growth. In rupee terms, the growth for the quarter came in at 8.4% quarter-on-quarter and 30.3% year-on-year. In constant currency terms, the growth for the quarter was 7.8% quarter-on-quarter and 20.8% year-on-year. The EBIT margin for the quarter came in at 15%, translating to an EBIT growth of 1.6% quarter-on-quarter and 19.5% year-on-year. The operating profit after tax for the quarter came in at 10.6%, translating to a PAT growth of 2.5% quarter-on-quarter and 5% year-on-year. The reported profit after tax for the quarter came in at 7.5%. I would like to point out that the reported PAT includes exceptional one-time expenses as part of Nagarro acquisition, resulting in approximately 3.1% impact for the quarter. Vinit, our CFO, will provide a detailed colour on the financials and margin movement later in this call. Coming to the order book for the quarter, the total contract value for the quarter stood at USD 633.5 million, with total contract value of new bookings coming in at USD 367.1 million. The annual contract value of bookings for this quarter was USD 481 million, out of which the annual contract value from new bookings contributed to USD 262.3 million. To remind everyone, both TCV and ACV numbers include all bookings, small and large, renewals as well as new bookings across existing and newer customers. Also, as highlighted in our earlier calls, our revenue conversion on a quarterly basis is a function of ACV bookings closed in previous quarters, as well as the conversion from multi-year deals booked in previous years, which are included in our total contract value or TCV bookings that we announce on a quarterly basis.

Let me now take you through the financial highlights for the quarter. Q2 FY27 revenue stood at USD 487.6 million, registering a year-on-year growth of 20%. In rupee terms, it translates to Rs.46,639 million, a growth of 30.3% year-on-year. EBIT for this quarter was Rs.6,977.2 million, translating to a growth of 19.5% year-on-year. EBIT margins for Q2 FY27 came in at 15%, 130 basis points declined year-on-year. I will now talk about some operational updates for this quarter. At the end of Q2 FY27, our total headcount stood at 29,598, an increase of 958 from previous the quarter. Utilization stood at 85.8%, down 70 basis sequentially, primarily reflecting proactive hiring to support the ramp-up of large deals. Trailing 12-months attrition stood at 11.9% compared to 12.3% in the previous quarter. Let me now give you quarter-on-quarter EBIT margin walkthrough. First, headwinds: As you would remember, this is the quarter when we have the yearly wage hike coming into effect. This impacted our margins by 180 basis points. However, lower ESOP costs enabled us to absorb part of this impact, leaving us with a net impact of 140 basis points. Lower utilization led to a 20 basis impact on our EBIT margins. The large deal that we have announced in the previous quarter included end-to-end takeover of the engineering roadmap of portfolio of 20 products across development, sustenance engineering, customer support, along with associated third-party licenses and cloud spend. This investment in the third-party tools and licenses led to an increase in the quarterly amortization of approximately USD 4 million, which had an impact of 90 basis points on our Q2 EBIT margin. The plan is to leverage FinOps and AI-led engineering roadmap to optimize the spend across people, tools, and cloud infrastructure in this large deal going forward. As we optimize the spend and our revenue scales in future, the impact on our margins will gradually reduce. Tailwinds: Lower ESOP SG&A expenses and favorable currency moments delivered a combined EBIT benefit of 150 basis points. Net impact taken together these headwinds and tailwinds resulted in a 100 basis point quarter-on-quarter decline in EBIT margin.
